finalists.label: Myocardial Infarction with Cardiac Rupture
finalists.why: This candidate is supported by severe chest pain radiating to the back, occlusive thrombosis of the tiny distal left circumflex artery, and pericardial effusion with contrast leakage from myocardium to pericardial cavity.

finalists.label: Myocardial Infarction
finalists.why: This candidate is supported by severe chest pain lasting for 4 hours, elevated cTnT, ST-segment elevation in inferior-posterior leads, and occlusive thrombosis of the tiny distal left circumflex artery.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of pericardial effusion and contrast leakage from myocardium to pericardial cavity, as evidenced by the Coronary Angiography and Computed Tomography Angiography, decided the final comparison in favor of Myocardial Infarction with Cardiac Rupture.
